input:
You are pawn_d2, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 26. the team planned dxc5 (pawn_d2), but bishop_f1 (greed) sent Bxg6 instead, and that move was played, costing 108 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 14. the team planned Kd1 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kd2 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.
- On move 17. the team planned Kd1 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Ke2 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is the planned move and your piece is the one named; if you are threatened or see a capture but it is not the plan, post it in chat instead of sending it, and otherwise stay silent.
- Before sending your piece's move, write the exact planned move from chat (e.g. 'Kd1') next to your intended move and send only if the two strings match character for character; if they differ, or your piece is not the one named, send nothing and post in chat instead.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Only the piece named in the team's agreed plan may send a move, and it must send exactly the planned move; every other agent, even if threatened or offered a capture, must post that in chat and send nothing, and the named piece must re-check its own move against the plan string immediately before sending.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
